summary.title: Think Like (a) Git
summary.one_liner: Learn Git by understanding its underlying model: commits as graph nodes, references as labels that make commits reachable, and how branches, merges, rebase, and cherry-pick work.
keywords: why is git hard to learn
takeaways: Git's commits form a directed graph, and references (branches, tags) are labels that keep commits reachable.
Branches act as savepoints, and merges and rebases become easier to reason about once you see them as graph operations.
git cherry-pick can be used to simulate git rebase for individual commits.
Visualizing the repository graph helps explain what Git commands like merge and rebase actually do.
summary.summary: Think Like (a) Git is a tutorial site aimed at people who find Git hard to learn. It builds understanding from first principles, starting with an introduction to graph theory (nodes, edges, labels, directed graphs, reachability) and then applying those ideas to Git repositories. The later sections cover references, garbage collection, branches as savepoints, testing merges, rebase, cherry-picking, and a mnemonic for git rebase arguments. The page text is only the outline and introduction, so the specific depth of each section could not be verified from it.
